## Context / Problem
Each gate answers "enabled? / what ref? / fail mode on error?" separately. Plan-review claim,
plan-review close and the completion verifier share `gates.gate_enabled`
(`src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:96`), which is tri-state and catches **`ConfigError` only**,
printing a stderr warning on an unreadable config (`gates.py:127-138`); code review has its own
two-state `code_review_enabled` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:277`) which catches
bare `Exception`, returns `False`, and warns nothing (`gate_dispatch.py:283-286`) — the only
broad-except `verify.*` read in the tree. Error posture differs: the claim gate exits 1;
plan-review-close returns an `unavailable` dict (`gates.py:286,292-297`); the completion gate maps
the error through `failure.outcome_of` (`src/rebar/llm/failure.py:548`) to exit 11 or 1 at
`close_precheck.py:694-696`; code review returns INDETERMINATE.

**Ref resolution is already uniform** — every gate, the completion gate included, resolves through
`gate_source.resolve_gate_handle` (`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:76`); the completion path reaches
it at `src/rebar/llm/completion.py:149` via `close_autoresume.py:235`. An earlier revision of this
plan claimed the completion gate BYPASSES the resolver at `close_autoresume.py:141`; that is
false. Line 141 is `resolve_ref(ref or "HEAD", root, fetch=False)` inside `_reusable_attested_pass`
— a cache-hit equality check comparing the close target against the signed `verified-at-sha`, not
gate source selection. Routing THAT through `resolve_gate_handle` would let the reuse check honour
`REBAR_GATE_REF` and accept a certified PASS pinned to a DIFFERENT sha than the one being closed.

What differs between gates is not the resolver but the **arguments**: the completion gate pins
`source="attested"`, `ref=(ref or "HEAD")`, `fetch=False` deliberately (epic `raze-vet-ditch` S4,
rationale at `close_autoresume.py:225-234`) so the verdict is reproducible, branch-independent and
signable as a `verified-at-sha` the child-closure gate can trust. That pinning is load-bearing and
is **not** changed here.

In CI, "this change predates the gate script" is a shell guard repeated **24 times** across
`.github/`, not twelve: `_build-and-test.yml:145,159,181,195,210,288,377,570`;
`_optionality.yml:108,114,133`; `_mutation.yml:64`; plus `.github/actions/docs-gates/action.yml`
x10 and `gerrit-verify.yaml:323,332`. Bug `sapphire-vulnerable-fruitfly` added one and
`anxious-resistant-urson` was a missing one.

## Approach
Add `src/rebar/_commands/gate_policy.py` with
`resolve(gate, *, repo_root, ticket_id, ref=None) -> GateDecision(enabled, ref, sha, fail_mode)`
where `fail_mode` is declared per gate (`OPEN_WARN`, `CLOSED_EXIT1`,
`CLOSED_EXIT11_IF_RETRYABLE`, `INDETERMINATE`) and all four callers consume it.

`code_review_enabled` **keeps its name, its `repo_root`-only signature, its broad
`except Exception`, and its silent `False`** — it is re-expressed as a thin wrapper over
`gate_policy.resolve(...)` whose declared `fail_mode` is INDETERMINATE/silent. Routing it through
`gate_enabled` instead would change three observable behaviours: narrow the catch to `ConfigError`
(so a non-ConfigError would crash code review rather than degrade it), add a stderr warning on
every unreadable-config code review, and demand a `ticket_id` that code review — which dispatches
against a CHANGE, not a ticket — has no source for.

The completion gate's ref handling is unchanged.

Replace the twelve in-scope predates guards with
`.github/actions/skip-if-predates-gate/action.yml`. **A composite action cannot abort a caller's
`run:` block** (`uses:` cannot appear mid-`run:`, and a composite exiting 0 does not terminate the
calling step), so each site becomes a guard step emitting a `present` output plus the existing work
under `if: steps.<id>.outputs.present == 'true'`. Four sites carry behaviour a bare skip would drop
and must be ported explicitly:
- `_mutation.yml:64` also writes `matrix={"shard":[]}` and `has-shards=false` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`
  on skip (pinned by `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:250-267`);
- `_optionality.yml:108,114` guard two generators **independently inside one step** per bug
  `5bc6-5496-4e17-403a` — a joint guard would silence the older check on every tree that has it;
- `_build-and-test.yml:181,195` use the inverted `[ -f ]/else` form with no `exit 0` and continue
  afterwards;
- `_build-and-test.yml:377` guards the DATA file `.github/git-version-floor.txt` via `$floorfile`
  and the step continues into a `sort -V` comparison that can `exit 1`.

`docs-gates/action.yml` (x10) and `gerrit-verify.yaml` (x2) are **out of scope** and keep their
inline guards; the acceptance greps are scoped accordingly.

Guard: `except Exception` around a `verify.*` config read appears only in `gate_policy.py` and
`gate_dispatch.py` (`gates.gate_enabled` keeps its narrow `except ConfigError`).

## Guard construction
Follow the guard-test construction rule in the parent epic `airborne-wellloved-kingfisher`: owner module exempt, match the constituent conjunction or AST shape named in Approach (or the definition count where no distinctive atom exists), `# <construct>-ok: <reason>` escape marker, and behaviour pinned only by the named existing tests.

## Scope
`src/rebar/_commands/gate_policy.py` (new), `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py`,
`src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/close_autoresume.py`,
`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py`, `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` (only if a read moves to a
string key — add/retarget the `# read-via:` markers at lines 159, 163, 172, 193),
`.github/actions/skip-if-predates-gate/action.yml` (new), `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`,
`.github/workflows/_optionality.yml`, `.github/workflows/_mutation.yml`,
`tests/unit/commands/test_gate_policy.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py`,
`tests/scripts/test_check_config_reads_heldout.py` (only if the markers move).

## Testing
Table test: for each gate x {enabled, disabled, unreadable config, resolver exception} the decision
and the exit/verdict equal today's — including that code review stays SILENT on an unreadable
config while the other three warn to stderr. Edge: a non-`ConfigError` from `compose_config` still
degrades code review to inert, and still propagates for the three `gate_enabled` gates.

Pinning: `tests/unit/test_gate_state_tristate_f5c4.py`,
`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_gate_unreadable_config_2091.py` (note the path: this file is
under `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/`, NOT `tests/unit/`),
`tests/unit/test_close_gate_ran_predicate_2091.py`,
`tests/unit/test_close_precheck_duplicate_link_c8fd.py`,
`tests/unit/test_close_precheck_message_fb8b.py`, `tests/unit/test_close_autoresume_b5f8.py`, and
the workflow-body tests from `sapphire-vulnerable-fruitfly` pass unchanged.

**Seam-liveness hazard:** 20 `monkeypatch.setattr(gate_dispatch, "code_review_enabled", ...)` sites
across 6 files and 24 `monkeypatch.setattr(_gates, "gate_enabled", ...)` sites across 20 files bind
these two symbols. If the callers switch to calling `gate_policy.resolve(...)` directly, every one
of those patches becomes **inert but still green** — the test keeps passing while exercising the
real config. A test asserting each patched symbol is the one the production path actually calls
guards against that.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every gate's observable behaviour for the four conditions (enabled / disabled / unreadable config / resolver exception) is unchanged, INCLUDING that code review degrades silently with a broad `except Exception` while the three `gate_enabled` gates warn to stderr and catch `ConfigError` only; checked by `tests/unit/commands/test_gate_policy.py`'s table test plus `pytest tests/unit/test_gate_state_tristate_f5c4.py tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_gate_unreadable_config_2091.py tests/unit/test_close_gate_ran_predicate_2091.py tests/unit/test_close_autoresume_b5f8.py`.
- [ ] The twelve in-scope predates guards are replaced and the out-of-scope ones are untouched; checked by `grep -c 'skip-if-predates-gate'` over the three workflow files summing to 12, and `grep -c 'change predates the gate'` returning 10 for `.github/actions/docs-gates/action.yml` and 2 for `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`.
- [ ] The mutation selector still emits `matrix={"shard":[]}` and `has-shards=false` on a tree lacking `scripts/mutation_gate.py`; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py::test_mutation_selector_skips_pre_gate_trees_without_weakening_current_trees` passing unchanged.
- [ ] `_optionality.yml`'s two doc generators remain INDEPENDENTLY guarded — a tree carrying `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` but not `scripts/gen_cli_help.py` still RUNS the reference check (the regression bug `5bc6-5496-4e17-403a` fixed); checked by a new case in `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` executing the step body in all four presence combinations.
- [ ] The completion gate still pins `source="attested"`, `ref=(ref or "HEAD")`, `fetch=False` and is NOT influenced by `REBAR_GATE_REF`; checked by a test that sets `REBAR_GATE_REF=origin/main` and asserts a `--ref`-less close still verifies and signs `verified-at-sha` against local `HEAD` (epic `raze-vet-ditch` S4).
- [ ] `gate_dispatch.code_review_enabled` and `gates.gate_enabled` are still the symbols the production paths call, so the existing monkeypatch seams stay live; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_ws4.py tests/unit/test_code_review_gate_session.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_close_gate.py tests/unit/commands/test_close_disposition.py` passing unchanged.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_config_reads.py` reports clean and `pytest tests/scripts/test_check_config_reads_heldout.py` passes — every `verify.*` flag the resolver consumes still has an attribute read or a `# read-via:` marker naming its real reader.
